flagged.evidence: The source note says: "If a resource with a condition isn't created, any resources that depend on that resource aren't created either, regardless of their own conditions." That supports the answer (False). What CloudFormation actually does is different. A Ref or DependsOn from a resource that remains in the template to a resource whose condition is false does not get skipped quietly. CloudFormation rejects it with "Template format error: Unresolved resource dependencies [X] in the Resources block of the template". The aws-cdk PR #13889 (https://github.com/aws/aws-cdk/pull/13889) says the Condition "is not compatible with the dependency clause, as the resource will not exist if the Condition is false". AWS's own example at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/conditions-section-structure.html avoids the problem: the Policy that refs Bucket uses CreateBucketPolicy, which includes the bucket's CreateBucket condition.
flagged.problem: The answer (False, the resource is not created) holds. The explanation says CloudFormation "skips" the dependent resource even when that resource's own condition is true, which teaches that the rest of the stack deploys normally. In practice an unguarded Ref to a resource that is not created makes the whole create or update fail at template validation. Developers fix it by giving the referencing resource the same condition or by using Fn::If. An expert would reject the explanation as written.
flagged.suggestedFix: Keep the statement (answer False) and replace the explanation with this (about 225 characters): "A false condition removes the referenced resource, so an unguarded Ref to it fails template validation with an Unresolved resource dependencies error. Give the referencing resource the same condition or wrap the Ref in Fn::If." Keep the Condition attribute URL and add the Conditions syntax page as context. If an official page that names the error cannot be cited, drop the card.

This also moves 1.1 from 4/6 to 5/5. Source: 'Unlike standard mode, adaptive mode can delay or block the initial request, not just retries, when throttling is detected.'
rewrite.statement: Adaptive retry mode in an AWS SDK rate-limits initial requests too once it detects throttling.
rewrite.explanation: Adaptive mode adds a per-client rate limiter driven by throttling responses, so it can hold back a first attempt, not only a retry. Standard mode never delays the initial request.

rewrite.reason: source_problem: the cited overview page never says what sign-in returns, and the old explanation called every token a JWT although refresh tokens are opaque. rewrite.reason: ambiguous: the old statement made S3 the actor that checks kms:Decrypt and implied a check on every download (S3 Bucket Keys skip repeat KMS calls). It now states the caller's requirement. Source: 'To download an object encrypted with an AWS KMS key, you need kms:Decrypt permissions for the key' and 'Amazon S3 sends the encrypted data key to AWS KMS in a Decrypt request.'
rewrite.statement: Amazon S3 GetObject on an SSE-KMS object needs the caller to hold kms:Decrypt on its KMS key.
rewrite.explanation: S3 sends the object's encrypted data key to AWS KMS in a Decrypt request during the download, so a caller with s3:GetObject but no kms:Decrypt on that key is denied.
rewrite.sourceTitle: Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)

rewrite.statement: AWS SAM CLI sam local start-api runs a function's Lambda authorizer locally before the function.

Statement and answer are unchanged.
rewrite.statement: AWS AppSync EvaluateMappingTemplate sends the evaluated request to the resolver's configured data source.
rewrite.explanation: EvaluateMappingTemplate renders a template against a mock context you supply and returns evaluationResult. It runs no request against the resolver's data source.

rewrite.sourceTitle: Testing and debugging resolvers in AWS AppSync (VTL)

rewrite.reason: explanation_error: the old explanation said CloudFormation 'skips' the dependent resource, which implies the rest of the stack deploys normally. In practice an unguarded Ref fails validation. No official page names that error, so the new explanation keeps only what the Condition attribute note supports ('If a resource with a condition isn't created, any resources that depend on that resource aren't created either, regardless of their own conditions'). That wording is true under both the documented and the observed behaviour. Statement and answer are unchanged.
rewrite.statement: AWS CloudFormation creates a resource whose Ref dependency has a condition that evaluates to false.
rewrite.explanation: CloudFormation creates a conditional resource only when its condition is true. A resource that depends on an uncreated resource can't be created either, whatever its own condition says.
rewrite.misconception: A true resource condition permits creation despite a referenced dependency being excluded by its condition.

Statement and answer are unchanged.

rewrite.explanation: ValidateTemplate checks that the template is valid JSON or YAML. Whether a named EC2 key pair exists comes to light when CloudFormation creates or updates the stack.
rewrite.misconception: Template validation verifies that resource property values identify existing resources in the target environment.

cards.reason: Both lenses keep. feature-retry-behavior.html: 'Unlike standard mode, adaptive mode can delay or block the initial request, not just retries, when throttling is detected'; 'The rate limiter operates per SDK client instance'; standard 'retry quota never delays or blocks the initial request'.

cards.statement: Amazon S3 GetObject on an SSE-KMS object needs the caller to hold kms:Decrypt on its KMS key.
cards.explanation: A caller needs kms:Decrypt on the object's KMS key as well as s3:GetObject, because that key protects the data key S3 stored with the object. Without it, the download is denied.
cards.reason: Both lenses flagged the editor's 'S3 sends the data key to KMS during the download' claim. I checked it myself. bucket-key.html says 'subsequent requests that take advantage of this bucket-level key do not result in AWS KMS API requests', and bucket-level keys are 'fetched at least once per requester'. The wording lens's fix ('S3 calls AWS KMS Decrypt on the caller's behalf') still implies a KMS call on every download, so I used the fact lens's explanation. It is true with or without Bucket Keys. UsingKMSEncryption.html: 'To download an object encrypted with an AWS KMS key, you need kms:Decrypt permissions for the key' and 'Amazon S3 stores the encrypted data key as metadata with the encrypted data.' The statement is unchanged; the explanation is 177 chars.
